issues.failure_explanation: Corollary 3.6 asserts that the circuit computes the two's complement addition $a \boxplus b$ of fixed-point dyadics $a \in \mathbb{F}_{n_1,m_1}$ and $b \in \mathbb{F}_{n_2,m_2}$. However, the proof simply passes the unshifted bit registers of $a$ and $b$ directly to the integer adder $\mathcal{Q}_{(+)}$ of Lemma 3.5. When $m_1 \neq m_2$, the least significant bits of the registers have different scales ($2^{-m_1}$ versus $2^{-m_2}$). Aligning the registers without shifting scales $b$ by $2^{m_2-m_1}$, computing $a + 2^{m_2-m_1}b$ instead of $a + b$. Moreover, the true sum $a \boxplus b \in \mathbb{F}_{\max\{n_1,n_2\}+1, \max\{m_1,m_2\}}$ can require more than $n_1+m_1+1$ qubits when $m_2 > m_1$ or $n_2 > n_1$. In Lemma 3.7 (step 5), this faulty adder is directly used with $m = m_1+m_2 > m_2$ to add $b \in \mathbb{F}_{n_2,m_2}$ to the partial affine sum, scaling the bias $b$ by $2^{-m_1}$ and corrupting the affine payoff evaluation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict Corollary 3.6 to the case of equal fractional lengths $m_1 = m_2$ (and $n_1 \geq n_2$), and in Lemma 3.7 pad the input bias $b$ with $m_1$ zero bits so that it is loaded in $\mathbb{F}_{n_2, m_1+m_2}$, matching the fractional precision of the accumulated affine product sum before addition.
issues.overall_effect: The affine sums computed in Lemma 3.7 and subsequent component evaluations in Proposition 3.8 and Proposition 3.10 compute incorrect affine values where the intercept $b$ is scaled by $2^{-m_1}$ instead of being added as $b$.
issues.title: Fixed-point addition circuit fails for operands with unequal fractional lengths
issues.why_classification: Padding the bias register and restricting the adder to equal fractional lengths is a contained, local modification of the circuit registers and complexity bookkeeping that avoids changing the overall architecture and preserves all convergence and complexity rates.

issues.failure_explanation: In equation (1057)-(1060) of the proof of Theorem 2.7, bounding $\mathfrak{s}^{-1} = \left(6\eps^{-1}(C_2^2d^22^{n_1+1})^3\right)^{1/2}$, the calculation incorrectly takes $\sqrt{(C_2^2 d^2)^3} = C_2 d$ rather than $C_2^3 d^3$. Consequently, $d$ instead of $d^3$ multiplies $(d^{5/2})^{3/2} = d^{15/4}$, yielding an erroneous bound $\mathfrak{s}^{-1} = O(d^{19/4}\eps^{-2}) = O(d^{4.75}\eps^{-2})$ instead of the correct $O(d^{27/4}\eps^{-2}) = O(d^{6.75}\eps^{-2})$. Because of this algebraic error, the query complexity in (48) is claimed to be $O(d^5 \eps^{-3} \ln(1/\alpha))$, whereas the method actually yields $O(d^{6.75} \eps^{-3} \ln(1/\alpha)) = O(d^7 \eps^{-3} \ln(1/\alpha))$, which cannot be bounded by $O(d^5)$. Similarly, the gate complexity in (47) is claimed to be $O(d^{\max\{12, 5+C_3\}})$, whereas $27/4 + 7 = 13.75$ requires an exponent of at least 14.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the calculation of $\sqrt{(C_2^2 d^2)^3}$ to $C_2^3 d^3$ in (1057)-(1060), yielding $\mathfrak{s}^{-1} = O(d^{27/4}\eps^{-2})$, and update the theorem bounds to $O(d^7 \eps^{-3} \ln(21/\alpha))$ applications of $\mathcal{A}$ and $O(d^{\max\{14, 7+C_3\}} \eps^{-3} (1+\log_2(d\eps^{-1}))^{\max\{4, 2C_3\}})$ elementary gates.
issues.overall_effect: The dimension exponents in the main complexity guarantees of Theorem 2.7 (the gate complexity bound (47) and query complexity bound (48)) are incorrect and unestablished as stated.
issues.title: Underestimated scaling parameter exponent leads to invalid query and gate complexity bounds
issues.why_classification: While the stated exponents of $d$ in the main theorem are invalidated and must be worsened from $d^5$ to $d^7$ (queries) and from 12 to 14 (gates), the central qualitative promise—that the algorithm breaks the curse of dimensionality by maintaining polynomial complexity in $d$ and $\eps^{-1}$—survives intact under standard re-derivation.
